"""Aspect-preserving material components and repeated horizontal controls for audio players and fuel dispensers."""
import numpy as np
import cv2


def machine_features(rgb):
    # Preserve shape while shrinking the longest side to 192 pixels; this resolves panels without square stretching.
    height,width = rgb.shape[:2]
    # The physical size of every pixel feature is referenced to a common longest image dimension.
    scale = 192/max(height,width)
    # Rounding keeps the shape-preserving thumbnail on integer pixel coordinates.
    a = cv2.resize(rgb,(max(1,round(width*scale)),max(1,round(height*scale))),interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA).astype(np.float32)/255
    # Equal-channel brightness separates dark audio panels from white dispenser enamel.
    gray = a.mean(axis=2)
    # Channel spread tolerates a fifth-range cast on nominally white paint or neutral equipment.
    spread = a.max(axis=2)-a.min(axis=2)
    r,g,b = a.transpose(2,0,1)
    # A third-range brightness captures deep gray/black audio cabinets and displays rather than merely shaded white paint.
    dark = (gray<1/3)&(spread<.20)
    # Bright neutral enamel includes silver-white pumps while excluding pale blue sky and brass.
    white = (gray>.60)&(spread<.20)
    # Strong red, blue or green enamel provides coloured cabinet candidates; visible channel gaps reject foliage-gray casts.
    paint = ((r>g+.15)&(r>b+.15)&(r>.4))|((b>r+.15)&(b>g+.05)&(b>.4))|((g>r+.10)&(g>b+.10)&(g>.35))
    # Close three-pixel interruptions from labels and reflections without bridging separate large objects.
    closed_dark = cv2.morphologyEx(dark.astype(np.uint8),cv2.MORPH_CLOSE,np.ones((3,3),np.uint8))
    # Morphological component geometry requires no stored prototypes and adapts to the current image.
    f = dict(wide_panel=0.0,tall_enamel=0.0,tall_white=0.0,tall_paint=0.0,tall_mixed=0.0,panel_area=0.0)
    # Components are checked for three semantic materials; the mask count is constant and each is computed just once.
    # Mixed white/red/blue enamel belongs to one cabinet despite painted colour bands; foliage-green is excluded.
    mixed = white|(paint&~((g>r)&(g>b)))
    # The same component geometry tests the full mixed-enamel cabinet as well as its separate materials.
    for name,mask in [('dark',closed_dark),('white',white.astype(np.uint8)),('paint',paint.astype(np.uint8)),('mixed',mixed.astype(np.uint8))]:
        # Labels split physically separate coherent material regions in the current photograph.
        count,labels,stats,centers = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask,8)
        # Candidate dimensions and areas are vectorised over components rather than over pixels.
        box = stats[1:].astype(np.float32)
        if len(box)==0:
            continue
        # Stats columns are x,y,width,height,area; actual image aspect is retained in the ratio.
        xx,yy,ww,hh,area = box.T
        # Material occupancy within the axis-aligned box rewards solid panels over branching vegetation and coats.
        fill = area/np.maximum(ww*hh,1)
        # Boxes at the frame boundary are often backgrounds, so give them half the closed-object evidence.
        interior = np.where((xx>0)&(yy>0)&(xx+ww<a.shape[1])&(yy+hh<a.shape[0]),1,.5)
        # An eighth of thumbnail area denotes a substantial cabinet panel rather than a logo or tiny display.
        size = np.minimum(area/(a.shape[0]*a.shape[1]/8),1)
        # Components near the centre are more likely the photographed machine than surrounding signs and walls.
        cx,cy = centers[1:].T
        # The broad half-frame radius makes centre preference gentle and independent of a particular composition.
        central = np.maximum(0,1-np.hypot(cx/a.shape[1]-.5,cy/a.shape[0]-.5))
        # A wide audio faceplate starts at a 3:2 ratio and becomes fully elongated at 5:2.
        wide = np.clip(ww/np.maximum(hh,1)-1.5,0,1)
        # Upright dispenser paint starts at 5:4 height-to-width and reaches full support at 9:4.
        tall = np.clip(hh/np.maximum(ww,1)-1.25,0,1)
        # Tiny hairline components receive no panel evidence; a twelfth-frame is a visibly broad material surface.
        broad = np.minimum(np.minimum(ww,hh)/(192/12),1)
        # Rectangularity, size, centrality and broadness must agree rather than compensating for one another.
        evidence = fill*size*interior*central*broad
        if name=='dark':
            # A wide dark region large enough to be the entire object supports a player over a small pump display.
            values = evidence*wide
            f['wide_panel'] = float(values.max())
            # Report the winning panel area to distinguish a resolved object from tiny display fragments.
            idx = int(np.argmax(values))
            f['panel_area'] = float(area[idx]/(a.shape[0]*a.shape[1]))
        else:
            # Tall neutral/coloured panels support dispenser cabinets but need rigid-structure corroboration externally.
            value = float((evidence*tall).max())
            f['tall_'+name] = value
            f['tall_enamel'] = max(f['tall_enamel'],value)
    # Standard finite differences measure repeated straight controls at the same aspect-preserving scale.
    gx = cv2.Sobel(gray,cv2.CV_32F,1,0,ksize=3)/8
    # The perpendicular gradient distinguishes horizontal dial rows from vertical cabinet sides.
    gy = cv2.Sobel(gray,cv2.CV_32F,0,1,ksize=3)/8
    # A twentieth-range derivative is a visible panel boundary, with a 2:1 orientation criterion allowing modest perspective.
    horizontal = ((abs(gy)>.05)&(abs(gy)>2*abs(gx))).astype(np.uint8)
    # A sixth of the image width is a long control row, grille line or deck edge rather than isolated letters.
    length = max(3,round(a.shape[1]/6))
    # Three-pixel closing repairs little gaps before selecting continuous horizontal traces.
    runs = cv2.morphologyEx(cv2.morphologyEx(horizontal,cv2.MORPH_CLOSE,np.ones((1,3),np.uint8)),cv2.MORPH_OPEN,np.ones((1,length),np.uint8))
    # The middle half-frame emphasises faceplate controls, avoiding roof/sign bands at image boundaries.
    lo,hi = a.shape[0]//4,3*a.shape[0]//4
    # Row support is the fraction of width occupied by long horizontal controls.
    profile = runs[lo:hi].mean(axis=1)
    # Three-pixel row dilation merges the two contrast sides of one thick control into a single band.
    bands = (profile>1/4).astype(np.uint8)
    # A one-dimensional connected-component count measures distinct rows rather than edge pixel totals.
    n,_,st,_ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(bands[:,None],8)
    # Four supported rows mean repeated controls or grille geometry; capping avoids rewarding arbitrary textural excess.
    f['control_rows'] = min((n-1)/4,1)
    # Repeated rows matter only when substantial long horizontal line area is present in the faceplate region.
    f['control_support'] = float(profile.mean())
    return f


def machine_adjustments(f):
    # A quarter-unit of conjunctive component support means several geometric/material requirements agree visibly.
    panel = min(f['wide_panel']/.25,1)
    # The same quarter-unit scale measures a coherent, broad, upright enamel cabinet.
    upright = min(f['tall_enamel']/.25,1)
    # Four distinct supported control rows contribute one vote; a wide panel supplies independent object-shape evidence.
    return dict(cassette_player=panel+f['control_rows'],gas_pump=2*upright)

s=Path('classify_v08.py').read_text()
s=s.replace(\"    # A coarser geometry stage supplies\", \"    # Pink skin retains blue relative to green unlike brass; tenth-frame area means substantial visible hands.\\n    pink=(r>g*1.15)&(g>b*1.05)&(b>g*.65)&(r>.45)&(gray>.30)&(np.ptp(a,axis=2)<.40)\\n    f['pink']=float(pink.mean())\\n    # A coarser geometry stage supplies\")
start=s.index('def scores(f):');end=s.index('\\n\\ndef predict',start)
new='''def scores(f):
    # Unit-range semantic evidence represents absence through clearly resolved presence, without learned calibration.
    def unit(x):
        # Clipping prevents huge background areas from compensating for a missing essential object property.
        return float(np.clip(x,0,1))
    # A tenth-frame long-boundary occupancy is substantial machine structure; half of all edges forming lines denotes rigidity.
    hor=unit(f['hline']/.10)
    # Upright support uses the same tenth-frame geometric occupancy scale.
    vert=unit(f['vline']/.10)
    # Straight run support is measured relative to half of the visible boundaries.
    rigid=unit(f['lines']/.50)
    # One fifth-frame extra lower detail means a strong sky-to-facade transition.
    facade=unit(f['facade']/.20)
    # A third frame of green means outdoor vegetation; tenth-frame pink means visible hands or a face.
    green=unit(f['green']/.30)
    # Human skin is supporting context for a held fish, not a standalone object cue.
    skin=unit(f['pink']/.10)
    # A quarter of the broad centre occupied by muted olive is a substantial fish-coloured body.
    olive=unit(f['olive']/.25)
    # The scale surface is comparatively smooth at a four-percent brightness-residual scale.
    scales=1-unit(f['olivefine']/.04)
    # Broad adjacent white/dark regions, each fifth-centre area, capture characteristic dog coat patches.
    coat=unit(f['whitec']/.20)*unit((f['brownc']+f['blackc'])/.20)
    # Two percent image area in contact with broad white interiors is resolved coat adjacency.
    adjacent=unit(f['broadadj']/.02)
    # Reflective brass must occupy a sixth-frame region and show five-percent fine highlight variation.
    brass=unit(f['brightgold']/.15)
    # Conditional high-frequency response records tubular/specular material independently of overall area.
    sparkle=unit(f['brightfine']/.05)
    # Most methods below are conjunctions: supporting context cannot replace an absent essential material or geometry cue.
    s={k:0.0 for k in CLASSES}
    # Fish needs olive body material, supported by either human skin or green surroundings and smooth scale material.
    s['tench']=olive*(max(skin,green)+scales)/2*(1-rigid/2)
    # Dog requires pale/dark coat with broad patch contact; dark brown adds support without replacing the coat.
    s['english_springer']=coat*(1+adjacent+unit(f['brownc']/.25))/3*(1-rigid/2)
    # Audio players require rigid broad horizontal structure plus a dark or neutral panel, with little facade/green evidence.
    s['cassette_player']=rigid*max(hor,unit(f['wide_panel']/.25))*max(unit(f['neutral']/.60),unit(f['blackc']/.30))*(1-facade/2)*(1-green/2)
    # Saw needs coherent coloured motor housing, dark equipment and visible contours; housing can be a resolved 1/64-frame patch.
    housing=max(unit(f['orangeblob']/(1/64)),unit(f['orange']/(1/32)))
    # Dark material and fine contours support a compact powered tool rather than a flat orange object.
    s['chain_saw']=housing*(unit(f['blackc']/.25)+unit(f['edge']/.40))/2*(1-rigid/2)
    # Church needs the lower detailed facade and upright structure, supported by sky or masonry colour.
    s['church']=facade*(1+vert)/2*max(unit(f['sky']/.40),unit(f['brown']/.25))
    # Horn requires both yellow metal and fine reflections; foliage, rigidity and a sky/facade arrangement lower confidence.
    s['french_horn']=brass*sparkle*(1-green/2)*(1-rigid/2)*(1-facade*unit(f['sky']/.30)/2)
    # Truck requires rigid horizontal body and cabin-above-chassis layout; an eighth-height separation supplies full layout evidence.
    chassis=unit(f['chassis_offset']/.125)
    # Green/edge details corroborate the outdoors machine, but neither can replace a physical horizontal body.
    s['garbage_truck']=rigid*hor*(1+chassis+unit(f['edge']/.40)+green)/4*(1-facade/2)
    # Pump requires rigid upright cabinet structure plus enamel, with an optional upper screen and tall-component confirmation.
    enamel=max(unit(f['whitec']/.30),unit(f['red']/.15),unit(f['tall_enamel']/.25))
    # A physical upright cabinet must exist; the screen is supporting evidence because some pumps show analog dials.
    s['gas_pump']=rigid*vert*enamel*(1+f['display']+unit(f['tall_enamel']/.25))/3*(1-facade/2)
    # Golf joins white surface with green lawn, supported by smooth blurred vegetation and few rigid outlines.
    white=unit(f['whitec']/.15)
    # Smooth lawn is substantial at one fifth-frame; white can occur anywhere for a small off-centre ball.
    lawn=unit(f['smoothgreen']/.20)*unit(f['ballwhite']/.05)
    # Essential lawn/white composition is distinct from an olive body with human skin.
    s['golf_ball']=max(green*white,lawn)*(1+unit(f['smooth']/.70))/2*(1-rigid/2)
    # Parachute requires smooth sky around the lower and side background; blue corroborates but cloudy sky remains possible.
    surround=unit(f['skylower']/.50)*unit(f['skysides']/.50)
    # Blue low down is strong aerial context, while a neutral surrounding field gets half that context vote.
    s['parachute']=surround*(1+unit(f['bluelower']/.30))/2*(1-rigid/2)*(1-facade)
    return s
'''

    # Most methods below are conjunctions: supporting context cannot replace an absent essential material or geometry cue.
    s={k:0.0 for k in CLASSES}
    # Fish needs olive body material, supported by either human skin or green surroundings and smooth scale material.
    s['tench']=olive*(max(skin,green)+scales)/2*(1-rigid/2)
    # Dog requires pale/dark coat with broad patch contact; dark brown adds support without replacing the coat.
    s['english_springer']=coat*(1+adjacent+unit(f['brownc']/.25))/3*(1-rigid/2)
    # Audio players require rigid broad horizontal structure plus a dark or neutral panel, with little facade/green evidence.
    s['cassette_player']=rigid*max(hor,unit(f['wide_panel']/.25))*max(unit(f['neutral']/.60),unit(f['blackc']/.30))*(1-facade/2)*(1-green/2)
    # Saw needs coherent coloured motor housing, dark equipment and visible contours; housing can be a resolved 1/64-frame patch.
    housing=max(unit(f['orangeblob']/(1/64)),unit(f['orange']/(1/32)))
    # Dark material and fine contours support a compact powered tool rather than a flat orange object.
    s['chain_saw']=housing*(unit(f['blackc']/.25)+unit(f['edge']/.40))/2*(1-rigid/2)
    # Church needs the lower detailed facade and upright structure, supported by sky or masonry colour.
    s['church']=facade*(1+vert)/2*max(unit(f['sky']/.40),unit(f['brown']/.25))
    # Horn requires both yellow metal and fine reflections; foliage, rigidity and a sky/facade arrangement lower confidence.
    s['french_horn']=brass*sparkle*(1-green/2)*(1-rigid/2)*(1-facade*unit(f['sky']/.30)/2)
    # Truck requires rigid horizontal body and cabin-above-chassis layout; an eighth-height separation supplies full layout evidence.
    chassis=unit(f['chassis_offset']/.125)
    # Green/edge details corroborate the outdoors machine, but neither can replace a physical horizontal body.
    s['garbage_truck']=rigid*hor*(1+chassis+unit(f['edge']/.40)+green)/4*(1-facade/2)
    # Pump requires rigid upright cabinet structure plus enamel, with an optional upper screen and tall-component confirmation.
    enamel=max(unit(f['whitec']/.30),unit(f['red']/.15),unit(f['tall_enamel']/.25))
    # A physical upright cabinet must exist; the screen is supporting evidence because some pumps show analog dials.
    s['gas_pump']=rigid*vert*enamel*(1+f['display']+unit(f['tall_enamel']/.25))/3*(1-facade/2)
    # Golf joins white surface with green lawn, supported by smooth blurred vegetation and few rigid outlines.
    white=unit(f['whitec']/.15)
    # Smooth lawn is substantial at one fifth-frame; white can occur anywhere for a small off-centre ball.
    lawn=unit(f['smoothgreen']/.20)*unit(f['ballwhite']/.05)
    # Essential lawn/white composition is distinct from an olive body with human skin.
    s['golf_ball']=max(green*white,lawn)*(1+unit(f['smooth']/.70))/2*(1-rigid/2)
    # Parachute requires smooth sky around the lower and side background; blue corroborates but cloudy sky remains possible.
    surround=unit(f['skylower']/.50)*unit(f['skysides']/.50)
    # Blue low down is strong aerial context, while a neutral surrounding field gets half that context vote.
    s['parachute']=surround*(1+unit(f['bluelower']/.30))/2*(1-rigid/2)*(1-facade)
    return s
'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:];Path('classify.py').write_text(s)

"""Diagnostic analytic canopy-and-small-payload relation on a single photograph."""
import numpy as np
import cv2


def payload_relation(rgb):
    # A 160-square thumbnail shares the fixed image fractions used by the aerial-context probe.
    a=cv2.resize(rgb,(160,160),interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA).astype(np.float32)/255
    # Arithmetic brightness supplies orientation-independent local-contrast measurements.
    gray=a.mean(axis=2)
    # Three-tap unit-scaled Sobel derivatives reject textured border samples when estimating the sky backdrop.
    gx=cv2.Sobel(gray,cv2.CV_32F,1,0,ksize=3)/4
    # The orthogonal derivative treats all edge directions equally.
    gy=cv2.Sobel(gray,cv2.CV_32F,0,1,ksize=3)/4
    # Border strips each span a sixteenth-frame, broad enough for robust color medians without much subject intrusion.
    border=np.zeros(gray.shape,dtype=bool)
    # Symmetric strips sample the background on every side.
    border[:10]=True
    # The lower border often contains sky below a suspended canopy.
    border[-10:]=True
    # Both side borders can corroborate neutral sky in addition to blue sky.
    border[:,:10]=True
    # The last side is sampled identically to the first.
    border[:,-10:]=True
    # A twentieth-range derivative denotes smooth sky rather than object texture.
    smooth=np.hypot(gx,gy)<.05
    selected=a[border&smooth]
    if len(selected)==0:
        return 0.0
    # This single image supplies its own median backdrop colour; no training summaries are stored.
    background=np.median(selected,axis=0)
    # A two-pixel blur and sixth-range difference retain broad fabric and payload material while suppressing thin strings.
    distance=np.max(abs(cv2.GaussianBlur(a,(0,0),2)-background),axis=2)
    # Same-colour smooth background must occupy much of both the lower field and the border to establish suspension in air.
    sky=(distance<1/6)&smooth
    # A bright neutral or bluish backdrop is accepted; warm/green backdrop excludes ordinary lawn and indoor tan walls.
    skycolour=background.mean()>.35 and background[2]>background[0]-.08 and background[2]>background[1]-.08
    # Two fifths of the lower field and half the border must be smooth matching sky, independently of foreground shape.
    if not skycolour or sky[80:].mean()<.4 or sky[border].mean()<.5:
        return 0.0
    # Five-pixel opening disconnects thin suspension lines from the broader canopy and hanging body.
    mass=cv2.morphologyEx((distance>1/6).astype(np.uint8),cv2.MORPH_OPEN,cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE,(5,5)))
    # Component geometry comes only from this image's mask; no cross-image clustering is performed.
    n,labels,stats,centres=cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mass,8)
    # Ignore components under eight pixels, smaller than a resolved payload.
    keep=stats[1:,cv2.CC_STAT_AREA]>=8
    # Retain the full geometry rows of resolved components for pairwise relational tests.
    q=stats[1:][keep].astype(np.float32)
    if len(q)<2:
        return 0.0
    # Keep at most the sixty-four largest components, bounding pairwise work without selecting class exemplars.
    q=q[np.argsort(q[:,cv2.CC_STAT_AREA])[-64:]]
    # Coordinates and dimensions express the actual silhouettes after strings have been suppressed.
    x,y,w,h,area=q.T
    # Canopies are broad compared with their payload and need at least a sixth-frame span; near-round fabric remains allowed.
    canopy=(w>160/6)&(h<w*1.5)&(area>80)&(y+h/2<160*.6)&(y+h<160)
    # A compact person/package is narrower and smaller than the canopy above it, without requiring learned body proportions.
    small=(w[None,:]<w[:,None]/3)&(h[None,:]<h[:,None])&(area[None,:]<area[:,None]/3)
    # A positive vertical gap shows the suspension region rather than two adjacent patches inside one solid object.
    below=y[None,:]>y[:,None]+h[:,None]+2
    # Suspension length up to one and a half canopy widths accommodates both short and long visible lines.
    close=(y[None,:]-(y[:,None]+h[:,None]))<w[:,None]*1.5
    # The payload must project within the canopy's horizontal footprint.
    cx=x+w/2
    aligned=(cx[None,:]>x[:,None])&(cx[None,:]<x[:,None]+w[:,None])
    # Independent canopy, relative size, vertical gap and alignment tests must agree for a relation to exist.
    return float(np.any(canopy[:,None]&small&below&close&aligned))
# Machine v3: aspect-preserving panels and control rows

Task scope: train only, no viewer, no validation, no fitting or parameter search. Frozen reference is classify_v06.py. Only two fixed full-training candidate rule effects were measured. Feature summaries informed conceptual changes, but no data-derived arrays or automatically chosen numbers enter machine_v3.py. Main classifier and NOTES.md were not edited.

## Teacher consultation first

machine_teacher_v3.py selected the first four training pumps frozen v06 calls cassette, and the first four cassettes frozen v06 calls cassette. Teacher correctly labels all eight originals. Grayscale retains every label, supporting geometry rather than specific paint colours as the main distinction. Stretching width by two loses one pump but no cassette; stretching height by two loses two cassettes but no pump. Thus preserving physical object aspect is worth trying. Mean conv3/conv5 activation was examined, but no activation values or teacher parameters enter the features.

Four pump failures examined: ILSVRC2012_val_00015654.JPEG, n03425413_10387.JPEG, n03425413_13096.JPEG, n03425413_13403.JPEG. Four cassette controls: ILSVRC2012_val_00017463.JPEG, n02979186_11197.JPEG, n02979186_12705.JPEG, n02979186_13096.JPEG. All paths are under data/train. Full intervention output is machine_teacher_v3.log.

## Two independently designed feature ideas

1. Aspect-preserved material components. Resize longest side to192 preserving aspect. Detect neutral dark panels and bright/coloured enamel components. A solid wide dark region supports an audio faceplate; a solid tall white/red/blue region supports a dispenser body. Geometry uses connected-component rectangularity, substantial eighth-frame material area, a gentle centre preference, image-border penalty and component breadth. A mixed-enamel union was added before rule trials because red/white stripes are one physical cabinet despite different paint colour, while foliage-green is excluded from this union.
2. Repeated horizontal control rows. Extract long horizontal derivatives in the middle half-height; require quarter-width supported rows and count up to four distinct bands. Rows of controls/grilles are a player property beyond simply having some horizontal boundaries.

All constants describe image fractions, visible channel separations or geometric aspect ratios. The feature code contains no training summaries. Object components, not stored exemplars, are recomputed from each new image.

## Separability measured before rules

All505 training images processed by machine_v3_analysis.py. The following hand-specified diagnostic triggers were measured (not searched):

| Feature | Cassette | Pump | Truck | Church | Dog | Horn | Saw | Golf | Para | Tench |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Wide dark panel >.25 conjunctive support |7|0|2|1|0|0|1|2|1|0|
| Tall enamel >.25 conjunctive support |1|6|0|0|0|0|0|0|1|1|
| Four control rows (control_rows>.75) |16|5|5|1|0|3|1|2|2|0|
| Control support >.15 image-width fraction |2|0|0|0|0|0|0|0|0|0|

Median tall-enamel response cassette .001 vs pump .069; median wide-panel cassette .018 vs pump .006. These diagnostics show separation but sparse strong detections; do not turn all weak components into unconditional large votes.

Composition diagnostic: cassette4/50 portrait,40/50 landscape,6 square; pump27/50 portrait,22/50 landscape,1 square. Upright pumps tend to be framed vertically, but this is a weak photographic context cue, not object identity. Any orientation rule should be restricted to an already plausible player/pump contest. Typical camera orientation is temporally stable and does not require lookup.

## Fixed full-train rule trials (two total)

Both full train results and every changed class are in machine_v3_eval.log; per-image train-only feature diagnostics are machine_v3_train.json.

Frozen v06:197/505=39.01%. Per class in canonical order tench19,dog22,cassette27,saw6,church25,horn19,truck16,pump16,golf19,parachute28.

A: cassette gets one bounded wide-panel vote plus up to one control-row vote; pump gets two bounded tall-enamel votes. Both component votes saturate at .25 conjunctive support, representing visible agreement of material,size,shape and centrality requirements. Total197/505=39.01%, no improvement. Per class tench18,dog21,cassette32,saw6,church19,horn19,truck11,pump26,golf18,parachute27. Fixed7/broke2 cassettes; fixed11/broke1 pumps. Broke6 churches,5 trucks and one each dog,tench,golf,parachute. This is precisely why all new evidence needs context gating.

B: same A, plus one portrait vote for pump or one landscape vote for cassette, only if the frozen v06 winner was cassette or pump. Total202/505=40.00%, a small +5-image change without statistical significance. Per class tench18,dog21,cassette35,saw6,church19,horn19,truck11,pump28,golf18,parachute27. Relative to v06 fixed9/broke1 cassettes and fixed13/broke1 pumps, with the same other-class losses as A.

No third trial was run. A natural next integration would apply component/control adjustments only within an already plausible machine contest, protecting church/truck, but that is a recommendation rather than a measured result. The features may also help simply remove unjustified cassette votes where no broad dark panel or repeated controls exists. No threshold or vote search was performed after either candidate measurement.

## Deliverable

machine_v3.py has machine_features(rgb) and machine_adjustments(f). It imports only numpy/cv2, has no file reads, uses no learned model or stored data, and comments all substantive operations. Main classifier integration should inline the functions and context-gate additions. No validation was accessed. No independent whole-classifier claim is made.
# Aerial scene investigation v4

Train-only, no validation access, no main-file edits or parameter searches. All constants chosen for visible colour gaps, image fractions, and geometric relationships. A single fixed score candidate was tested against frozen `classify_v08.py` as requested; a separate payload relation received feature-trigger analysis only.

## Failure diagnosis

`sky_v4_probe.py` / `sky_v4_probe.log` list 22 missed training parachutes and 24 nonparachutes predicted parachute by v08. Several misses already have abundant lower/side gray sky but insufficient score: ILSVRC2012_val_00023107 lower .954/sides .976, _1517 .717/.987, _22668 .775/.989. Others have nearly horizontal fabric seams counted as manufactured rigidity: _11755 lines .337 with horizontal area .027 and vertical area .001; _26785 lines .552 with horizontal .025/vertical .001; _28095 lines .421 with horizontal .075/vertical0. Thus reducing every canopy to blue coverage, smoothness and generic long lines misses object relationships. Conversely studio or tinted backgrounds cause player/horn/golf false aerial decisions; some nonparachute blue regions are highly textured rather than sky.

## Fixed broad fabric/background candidate

`sky_v4.py` estimates this image's backdrop as median RGB of smooth pixels along four border strips. It segments visible broad foreground differences, removes thin lines by a five-pixel opening, and tests a broad solid upper component floating above lower background. Relative brightness/color and background coverage gate its contribution. No numeric median is stored or pooled across images. `pendant` is a diagnostic sparse-below-body feature; the measured adjustment uses canopy support only (the original algebraic max with pendant was equivalent, as pendant is bounded by canopy).

`sky_v4_eval.py` ran all 505 train images. Median lower same-background smoothness was .692 for parachute, .377 golf, .339 audio, .293 horn, .246 saw, .205 pump, .197 truck/dog, .172 church, .161 fish. Median backdrop sky-colour acceptance was1 for parachute and0 for all other classes. However broad closed-canopy shape support was zero at the median for every class, including parachute.

Parachute28->29, dog22->21. Recovered n03888257_15735 from audio; broke dog n02102040_7517; also shifted already-wrong saw n03000684_4557 and church n03028079_15483 to parachute. This score candidate is rejected: no aggregate improvement.

Numeric component diagnosis (`sky_v4_components.py`) explains why a strongly horizontal silhouette is wrong for gray-sky misses. ILSVRC00023107 main foreground box42x41 and lower payload8x14; _1517 largest86x134; _22668 largest64x120 with separate37x46 upper component; _11755 broad component77x45 plus separate9x8 below. Some parachutes are near-round or connected to long suspension/person structure, rather than isolated very wide masses. External contour areas may include holes and were only diagnostic; connected-component pixel areas are used in the separate relation below.

## Separate canopy/payload relation feature

`sky_payload_v4.py` uses the same single-image smooth-border backdrop, accepts broad OR near-round fabric, and requires a distinct much smaller/narrower foreground component below the canopy within its horizontal span. The gap represents suspension; five-pixel opening removes the joining thin lines. Relative geometric tests require no stored prototype. It independently gates on sky-colour backdrop with smooth matching material covering at least two fifths lower field and half border.

`sky_payload_v4_eval.py`, all505 train trigger counts: parachute11/50, saw2/50, dog1/50, horn1/50, golf1/50; zero audio/church/truck/pump/fish. Triggered parachutes: ILSVRC2012_val_00015689, ILSVRC2012_val_00023107, n03888257_11755, _14703, _15735, _1797, _24519, _36265, _42945, _54265, _60113. Four are missed by v08: ILSVRC00023107, _11755, _15735, _24519. Nonparachute triggers: saw n03000684_13684 and _4557; dog n02102040_7517; horn n03394916_15755; golf n03445777_10719. This is low recall but more selective than broad-shape support. It has NOT been tested as an additional score candidate; parent retains that choice. Some golf ball/tee arrangements can satisfy canopy/payload geometry, so independent sky gating remains necessary.

## Teacher interventions on missed gray-sky scenes

`sky_v4_teacher.py` examines six missed parachutes and two falsely aerial studio backgrounds. It compares original, foreground-only (background replaced neutral), background-only (foreground replaced estimated sky), global blur, and inspects conv3 summary. No teacher outputs were fitted.

All six original parachutes are correctly identified by the teacher. Foreground-only preserves five of six; background-only preserves four of six; global blur preserves four of six. In detail:

- ILSVRC00023107: target margin1.84 original,1.35 object-only,.31 background-only,.19 blur.
- _11755:2.78 original,2.56 object-only; background-only becomes golf; blur retains para1.18.
- _1517: original para margin.22, object-only horn, background-only audio, globalblur audio. Both object detail and context matter in this difficult case.
- _22668:1.80 original,2.09 object-only,.20 background-only; globalblur audio. Its resolved foreground structure is needed beyond smooth sky.
- _24519:2.48 original,2.27 object-only,1.39 background-only,2.16 blur.
- _26785:1.27 original,.04 object-only,2.50 background-only,1.28 blur; backdrop context dominates this case.

Falsely aerial audio n02979186_11883 is correctly audio originally; object-only becomes golf, background-only remains audio, globalblur remains audio. Horn n03394916_35688 is correctly horn originally; object-only becomes para, background-only becomes audio, globalblur remains horn. The teacher combines foreground and photographic context in ways that smooth sky coverage alone cannot reconstruct.

Recommendation: reject the measured broad-fabric score candidate. The more selective separate-payload relation is available for root review, with explicit low recall and five false material arrangements. No validation passes spent.

# Analytic texture hierarchy investigation v3

Train-only; no validation access; no teacher constants copied; no fitted parameters or automated parameter searches. Parent allowed at most two classifier experiments against frozen `classify_v06.py`, and exactly two were measured. No main classifier or NOTES edits.

## Mechanism and implementation

`texture_v3.py` computes a fixed Gaussian octave bank at one, two, four and eight thumbnail pixels, conditional band contrast for white/green/olive/warm material and image centre, thin white glints adjoining warm material, and analytic Hessian line ridges in warm material. All constants express chosen image scales, visible colour gaps, or geometric principal-curvature ratios; all nontrivial lines commented. The implementation contains no stored statistics, models, templates, or arrays computed across images.

Teacher evidence motivating it: prior `round_analysis.py` / `round_causal_v2.py` show global blur destroys horn decisions but preserves the first four golf decisions, with improved golf margins in three. Bright-warm selective blur weakens all four horns. Root's tile-shuffle experiment shows horn evidence survives 16-pixel tile disorder, whereas golf fails at 32-pixel tile disorder. Hence local warm texture and broad lawn/white composition are plausible distinct mechanisms; dimples/indiscriminate circle methods were already shown unhelpful and were not retried.

## All-train diagnostic feature measurements

`texture_v3_probe.py` runs all 505 training images and reports medians plus fixed semantic trigger rates. Numerical summaries are diagnostic only, not embedded classifier tables.

- Warm ridge whole-image area median: horn .079, dog .040, saw .039, church .035, fish .032, pump .022, golf .013, truck .011, audio .008, parachute .006. Conditional ridge fraction median: horn .474, church .418, pump .393, truck .375, saw .358, audio .331, dog .325, parachute .299, fish .268, golf .199. Promising in isolation but substantial overlap.
- Trigger warm ridge area>.03 AND conditional ridge fraction>.25: horn38/50, church30/55, saw22, fish22, dog17, pump16, audio11, parachute8, golf7, truck7. These are not selective enough on their own.
- Narrow warm-adjacent white glints>.03: horn21, dog22, saw21, church19, fish16, truck14, pump14, audio6, parachute4, golf3. Rejected as nonseparating.
- Green fine-to-medium octave ratio median: golf .848, fish1.316, church1.324, truck1.085, saw.976, dog.879, pump.881, audio.630, horn.536, parachute.752. Green area>.20 AND white area>.02 AND green fine/medium ratio<1 fires golf8, pump3, dog2, parachute2, saw1, fish1, truck1, zero others. Weak recall, mostly duplicates the existing smooth-lawn cue.
- Warm conditional fine residual>.04 AND fine residual>medium octave contrast fires horn35, church26, saw15, truck15, parachute12, pump11, dog8, golf7, audio6, fish3. Too many backgrounds/other objects.

## Two fixed classifier experiments

`texture_v3_experiments.py` compares both independently with frozen v06. Baseline was exactly reproduced: 197/505=39.01%, per-class successes in standard class order [19,22,27,6,25,19,16,16,19,28]. Its cached diagnostic feature file is train-only and is never part of the delivered classifier.

Experiment 1 adds one corroborating horn vote = clip(warm_ridge_area/.10)*clip(warm_ridge_fraction/.50). A tenth-frame of resolved tube ridges and half of warm pixels carrying tube texture are deliberately chosen saturation scales. Result 194/505=38.42%; per-class [18,20,27,5,24,23,15,16,18,28]. Four horns recovered, seven other correct decisions broken. Example newly correct horns: n03394916_20777, _28033, _33177, _35748. False material matches include warm dogs, saws and brick. No further parameter tuning attempted.

Experiment 2 adds two golf context votes = 2*clip(green_area/.20)*clip(white_area/.10)*(1-clip(green_fine_contrast/.04)). These scales mean a visible fifth-frame lawn, a tenth-frame bright subject and under-four-percent fine material contrast. Result 194/505=38.42%; per-class [18,22,27,6,25,19,12,16,22,27]. Three golf images recovered (n03445777_13874, _2597, _7666); six other correct decisions broken, including four trucks. No further parameter tuning attempted.

Both changes are rejected. Differences are small relative to measurement power, and neither establishes useful aggregate improvement. This investigation does not justify adding a larger bank of texture scores to the main classifier.

## Targeted teacher and feature interventions

`texture_v3_teacher.py` examines two newly correct horns, two newly correct golf images and two trucks broken by experiment 2. Each is tested original, warm-only blur, green-only blur, global blur; conv3 average is inspected as well as decisions/margins. No outputs are fitted.

- Horn n03394916_20777: warm-ridge area .188->.075 under warm-only blur, teacher target margin3.74->.51; global blur ridge .009 and teacher predicts parachute. Horn _28033: ridge .105->.047, teacher margin3.04->1.66; global blur ridge0 and predicts golf. This is causal support for local reflective detail but not sufficient class specificity.
- Golf n03445777_2597 and _7666 retain golf under every intervention. Green-only blur lowers green fine contrast .008->.002 and .005->.002 respectively without harming the teacher's golf evidence. Their useful evidence is broader than fine grass texture.
- Truck n03417042_11318: original truck margin4.75; green-only blur margin2.40; global blur predicts golf (margin -3.12 for truck). Truck _15908: green-only blur barely changes truck margin3.53->3.61; global blur predicts golf (truck margin -3.33). Therefore a blurred-lawn cue must be paired with stronger resolved manufactured-object evidence. Merely strengthening the golf blur bonus incorrectly overrides that evidence.

Recommendation: retain v06 over these two trials. A new strategy needs object relations or independently selective material structure; the extra texture summaries tested here duplicate existing coarse evidence and shift confusions rather than resolve them.
"""Nonlearned material texture, depth-of-field and reflective ridge evidence."""
import numpy as np
import cv2


def texture_features(rgb):
    # A 160-square thumbnail places fur fibres, lawn texture and brass highlights on fixed pixel scales.
    a=cv2.resize(rgb,(160,160),interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA).astype(np.float32)/255
    # RGB opponency isolates warm metal, olive fish, lawn and white material without learned transforms.
    r,g,b=a.transpose(2,0,1)
    # Equal primary weights make all derivative values fractions of brightness range.
    gray=a.mean(axis=2)
    # Warm metal tolerates dark golden reflections; colour ratios reject strongly reddish fur and vivid foliage.
    gold=(r>b+.10)&(g>b+.05)&(g>r*.7)&(g<r*1.05)&(g>.25)
    # White material includes moderate gray shade and allows a small fifth-range colour cast.
    white=(gray>.5)&(np.ptp(a,axis=2)<.2)
    # Lawn has a visible green excess over both competing channels.
    green=(g>r+.03)&(g>b+.03)
    # Olive fish material is darker and less green than grass, with red and green close in value.
    olive=(np.minimum(r,g)>b+.035)&(r>g-.025)&(r<g+.08)&(gray>.1)&(gray<.7)
    # A third-image central window keeps texture of the putative object separate from landscape borders.
    central=np.zeros(gray.shape,dtype=bool)
    # Central half-frame catches main object material while avoiding all four background corners.
    central[40:120,40:120]=True
    # A three-pixel opening preserves bright material interiors, removing isolated noise before identifying narrow glints.
    broadwhite=cv2.morphologyEx(white.astype(np.uint8),cv2.MORPH_OPEN,cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE,(9,9)))>0
    # Narrow white glints are common on brass tubing but broad white dog coats should not contribute.
    glint=white&~broadwhite
    # A five-pixel neighborhood asks whether white glints adjoin warm reflective metal.
    neargold=cv2.dilate(gold.astype(np.uint8),np.ones((5,5),np.uint8))>0
    # Whole-image glint area needs no learned normalization; broad-brass area remains separate for semantic gating.
    f=dict(warm_glint=float((glint&neargold).mean()),warm_area=float(gold.mean()),white_area=float(white.mean()),green_area=float(green.mean()))
    # Gaussian scales one, two, four and eight form an octave bank spanning fine fibres through broad photographic shapes.
    scales=[cv2.GaussianBlur(gray,(0,0),k) for k in (1,2,4,8)]
    # Absolute octave differences indicate how much contrast lies at each spatial scale.
    bands=[abs(gray-scales[0])]+[abs(scales[k]-scales[k+1]) for k in range(3)]
    for name,mask in [('white',white),('green',green),('olive',olive),('gold',gold),('centre',central)]:
        # A one-pixel denominator guard handles absent materials without affecting visible patches.
        den=max(int(mask.sum()),1)
        for k,band in enumerate(bands):
            # Conditional band contrast is material sharpness, independent of its total photographic area.
            f[name+'_band'+str(k)]=float((band*mask).sum()/den)
    # A one-pixel Gaussian scale supplies smooth second derivatives for bright/dark tube ridges.
    smooth=scales[0]
    # Standard three-tap Hessian entries use second central differences, never a learned kernel.
    hxx=cv2.Sobel(smooth,cv2.CV_32F,2,0,ksize=3)/4
    # Orthogonal curvature complements the first entry with identical physical units.
    hyy=cv2.Sobel(smooth,cv2.CV_32F,0,2,ksize=3)/4
    # Mixed curvature permits ridge orientation to be arbitrary, matching coiled brass tubes.
    hxy=cv2.Sobel(smooth,cv2.CV_32F,1,1,ksize=3)/4
    # Eigenvalue gap and trace analytically describe principal curvatures.
    gap=np.sqrt((hxx-hyy)**2+4*hxy*hxy)
    # Principal curvature pair detects one-dimensional tube ridges versus isotropic spots.
    lo,hi=(hxx+hyy-gap)/2,(hxx+hyy+gap)/2
    # A bright ridge bends downward strongly across its width and remains relatively flat along its length.
    brightridge=(lo<-.02)&(np.abs(hi)<np.abs(lo)/3)
    # Dark troughs between shiny tubes have the opposite curvature sign but the same 3:1 line character.
    darkridge=(hi>.02)&(np.abs(lo)<np.abs(hi)/3)
    # Both ridge signs contribute when co-located with warm metal; one fifty-th range curvature is visibly resolved.
    f['warm_ridge']=float((gold&(brightridge|darkridge)).mean())
    # Conditional ridge fraction describes metallic texture independently of how large the instrument is.
    f['warm_ridge_fraction']=float((gold&(brightridge|darkridge)).sum()/max(int(gold.sum()),1))
    # Material-scale contrast ratios characterize blurred background and sharp surface without any learned templates.
    f['green_fine_ratio']=f['green_band0']/(f['green_band2']+1e-6)
    # White fine-to-broad detail can describe a textured bright object on a smooth lawn; the guard affects blank regions only.
    f['white_fine_ratio']=f['white_band0']/(f['white_band2']+1e-6)
    return f

p=Path('classify.py');s=p.read_text();needle=\"    # A coarser geometry stage supplies\"
insert='''    # Coiled metal contains bright ridges and dark troughs: smooth one-pixel noise before analytic second derivatives.
    tubegray=cv2.GaussianBlur(gray,(0,0),1)
    # Standard second central differences measure horizontal curvature on unit brightness, divided by stencil mass four.
    hxx=cv2.Sobel(tubegray,cv2.CV_32F,2,0,ksize=3)/4
    # Vertical curvature uses the same analytic stencil and physical units.
    hyy=cv2.Sobel(tubegray,cv2.CV_32F,0,2,ksize=3)/4
    # Mixed curvature lets tube orientation be arbitrary around a coil.
    hxy=cv2.Sobel(tubegray,cv2.CV_32F,1,1,ksize=3)/4
    # Closed-form principal curvatures avoid any learned orientation filter bank.
    gap=np.sqrt((hxx-hyy)**2+4*hxy*hxy)
    # The trace plus/minus eigenvalue gap gives the two signed curvatures.
    lo,hi=(hxx+hyy-gap)/2,(hxx+hyy+gap)/2
    # Resolved ridges exceed two-percent curvature and are three times stronger across the tube than along it.
    ridge=((lo<-.02)&(abs(hi)<abs(lo)/3))|((hi>.02)&(abs(lo)<abs(hi)/3))
    # Warm reflective material includes darker gold shadows without accepting strongly red fur or green foliage.
    warm=(r>b+.10)&(g>b+.05)&(g>r*.7)&(g<r*1.05)&(g>.25)
    f['tuberidge']=float((warm&ridge).mean())
    # Conditional ridge coverage asks for tube structure within the material, rather than a large brown wall alone.
    f['tubefraction']=float((warm&ridge).sum()/max(warm.sum(),1))
'''
s=s.replace(needle,insert+needle)

p.write_text(s)

p=Path('NOTES.md');p.write_text(p.read_text()+'''\\nv17 measured train221/505=43.76%,37.0ms,no errors; crop gains dog+2,audio+2,horn+2,truck+6,pump+2,loses church2,golf3,saw1.\\n'''+Path('val_v17.log').read_text()+'''\\nBest44.65%, still below target. v18 intentional two-view architecture: preserve central-square object scale/shape while measuring full-frame sky/lawn/facade context once for all classes. Existing full-frame coarse geometry already supplies a lower-detail contrast; use it for facade. The shared full-frame thumbnail/gradient stage provides outdoor colours, smooth lawn, surrounding sky and canopy/payload relation. This is geometric design, not score fitting.\\n''')
p=Path('classify.py');s=p.read_text();needle=\"    # A coarser geometry stage supplies\"
insert='''    # A second full-frame thumbnail supplies scene context without stretching the central object used above.
    scene=cv2.resize(rgb,(160,160),interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA).astype(np.float32)/255
    # Scene opponent channels locate foliage and sky around the object crop.
    sr,sg,sb=scene.transpose(2,0,1)
    # The full scene uses the same analytic HSV definitions as the object view, with no class-specific calibration.
    sh,ss,sv=cv2.cvtColor(scene,cv2.COLOR_RGB2HSV).transpose(2,0,1)
    # Mean scene brightness permits the same Sobel/texture scale as the object view.
    scenegray=scene.mean(axis=2)
    # Scene gradients distinguish smooth sky/lawn context from paint, lettering and foliage detail.
    sgx=cv2.Sobel(scenegray,cv2.CV_32F,1,0,ksize=3)/4
    # Orthogonal scene derivatives maintain orientation-independent smoothness evidence.
    sgy=cv2.Sobel(scenegray,cv2.CV_32F,0,1,ksize=3)/4
    # Euclidean gradient magnitude is shared by every context hypothesis.
    smag=np.hypot(sgx,sgy)
    # Global green, brown and blue are scene context; central material fractions above retain object-view proportions.
    f['green']=float(((sh>65)&(sh<170)&(ss>.20)).mean())
    # Warm masonry over the whole scene supports church context independently of the cropped subject.
    f['brown']=float(((sh>8)&(sh<48)&(ss>.22)&(sv<.65)).mean())
    # Use the same broad blue hue interval globally and at top/bottom, keeping aerial and building context comparable.
    sceneblue=(sh>175)&(sh<260)&(ss>.18)&(sv>.35)
    f['blue']=float(sceneblue.mean())
    # Top three-eighths corresponds to upper sky, while lower three-eighths locates aerial continuation below the subject.
    f['bluetop']=float(sceneblue[:60].mean())
    # Lower sky remains visible even if a central crop contains mostly fabric.
    f['bluebottom']=float(sceneblue[100:].mean())
    # Opponent-blue and neutral clouds require smoothness, rejecting blue lettering or textured white object surfaces.
    sceneopponent=(sb>sr+.04)&(sb>sg-.03)&(sb>.35)
    # Fifteen-percent saturation and above-midgray value admit bright overcast sky.
    scenecloud=(ss<.15)&(sv>.55)
    # Four-percent gradients denote smooth sky at this resolution.
    scenesky=(sceneopponent|scenecloud)&(smag<.04)
    f['skylower']=float(scenesky[80:].mean())
    # Side strips each occupy one eighth-frame, measuring background around the entire object.
    f['skysides']=float(np.concatenate((scenesky[:,:20].ravel(),scenesky[:,-20:].ravel())).mean())
    # Blue-only low and high context distinguishes aerial surroundings and outdoor vehicle scenes from studio white.
    f['bluelower']=float((sceneopponent&(smag<.04))[80:].mean())
    # Upper smooth blue counts as weak outdoor context for the manufactured-object contest.
    f['blueupper']=float((sceneopponent&(smag<.04))[:80].mean())
    # Full lawn retains depth-of-field context discarded when a large white ball fills the crop.
    f['smoothgreen']=float(((sg>sr+.03)&(sg>sb+.03)&(smag<.05)).mean())
    # Small neutral white subjects may be off-centre, so their supporting global area comes from the scene view.
    f['ballwhite']=float(((scenegray>.50)&(np.ptp(scene,axis=2)<.20)).mean())
    # Canopy/payload spatial relationships need the entire object rather than a square crop that might clip the lower body.
    f['payload']=payload_relation(scene,scenegray,smag)
'''
s=s.replace(needle,insert+needle)
s=s.replace(\"    f.update(cabinet=geo['cabinet'],display=geo['display'],chassis_offset=geo['chassis_offset'])\", \"    f.update(cabinet=geo['cabinet'],display=geo['display'],chassis_offset=geo['chassis_offset'])\\n    # The full frame's sky-to-ground transition measures facade context while central-crop long lines still describe object structure.\\n    f['facade']=geo['lowerdetail']\")
p.write_text(s)
PY
